original_query: SELECT NAME, DDEPTNO, COUNT(*) AS C FROM (SELECT NAME AS NAME, DEPTNO AS DDEPTNO FROM DEPT) AS t3 WHERE NAME = 'Charlie' GROUP BY GROUPING SETS((NAME, DDEPTNO), NAME)
rewritten_query:
SELECT NAME, DEPTNO AS DDEPTNO, COUNT(*) AS C
FROM DEPT
WHERE NAME = 'Charlie'
GROUP BY GROUPING SETS((NAME, DEPTNO), NAME)

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the redundant derived table t3, which only renamed columns and added no filtering or computation. The optimizer flattens it anyway, so eliminating it improves readability with zero semantic change.
The WHERE clause NAME = 'Charlie' is already minimal; it can be applied directly on the base table DEPT. No further predicate simplification needed.

Kept GROUPING SETS as a single-scan aggregation. Replacing it with UNION ALL would scan DEPT twice; adding a CTE is unnecessary since there is no repeated expensive computation. Optionally, a composite index on DEPT(NAME, DEPTNO) would let the planner use an index-only scan and avoid the Sort before GroupAggregate.
